Use triangle sums and a straight angle

question:
If \(\angle A = 20^\circ\) and \(\angle AFG =\angle AGF,\) then \(\angle B+\angle D =\)

[Figure 1](figures/2000_AMC_8_Q24_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Start with triangle \(AFG\), since its angle at \(A\) is known and its other two angles are equal. Those equal angles together measure \(180^\circ-20^\circ=160^\circ\), so
\[
\angle AFG=\angle AGF=80^\circ.
\]
In the figure, \(A,F,D\) lie on one straight line, with \(F\) between \(A\) and \(D\). Also, \(F,G,B\) lie on one straight line, with \(G\) between \(F\) and \(B\). Thus rays \(FG\) and \(FB\) are the same ray, while rays \(FA\) and \(FD\) point in opposite directions. Therefore
\[
\angle BFD=180^\circ-\angle AFG=100^\circ.
\]
The labeled angles at \(B\) and \(D\) are the other two angles of triangle \(BFD\). Its angle sum gives
\[
\angle B+\angle D=180^\circ-100^\circ=\boxed{80^\circ}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
